speaker: Doctor
text: Is the vaginal bleeding bright red or dark, and are you feeling any fetal movement right now? Given your previous C-section, have you had any episodes of tearing sensation in your abdomen?

text: My main symptom is Vaginal bleeding. I also have Severe abdominal pain, History of contractions that stopped, Previous cesarean delivery. You must output exactly the following diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gastroenteritis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severity of your symptoms and your history of a prior cesarean section, I suspect a uterine rupture rather than gastroenteritis. I need to confirm this immediately with a fetal heart rate monitor and an ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound; REQUEST TEST: Fetal_Monitoring.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Abdomen and Pelvis shows findings suggestive of a disruption in the uterine wall continuity adjacent to the scar from the previous cesarean section, with associated hemoperitoneum. Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring shows recurrent variable decelerations. Vital Signs indicate tachycardia (Pulse 110/min), hypotension (Blood Pressure 90/60 mm Hg), and normal respiratory rate (17/min). Abdominal examination reveals mild distension, decreased bowel sounds, tympanic sound on percussion, and diffuse abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding. Hemoglobin is decreased at 10.2 g/dL.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms a uterine rupture, which is a life-threatening emergency requiring immediate surgical intervention. DIAGNOSIS READY: Uterine Rupture
